newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stockholm, Danish bourses to merge trading systems.
newsitem.headline: Stockholm, Danish bourses to merge trading systems.

text.p: Stockholm Stock Exchange said on Thursday that it was to merge its trading system with that of the Copenhagen bourse.
"We will hold a press conference this afternoon about an agreement in principle regarding cooperation with the Copenhagen bourse," Lars Bredin, vice president of the Stockholm exchange, told Reuters.
"When bourses cooperate on something important it is about trading systems."
Bredin refrained from giving further details, referring to a press conference that the Copenhagen exchange will hold at 0830 GMT.

The Financial Times said on Thursday the two bourses would announce the deal on Thursday, quoting Stockholm bourse president Bengt Ryden as saying the common system would increase liquidity at both exchanges.
Sweden's 1996 share turnover was 918 billion Swedish crowns ($118.5 billion) while Copenhagen's volume was 217 billion Danish crowns ($33 billion).

Under the new scheme, to take effect from mid-1998, the Copenhagen exchange will replace its trading system with an upgraded version of the Stockholm system and the two exchanges will develop common regulations, the Financial Times said.
The tie-up would be the first such tie-up among Europen bourses and could mark the first step towards the creation of a pan-Nordic share market.
Ryden has previously talked about creating a pan-Nordic share market, extending to Oslo and Helsinki, but the Norwegians and Finns have been reluctant to join a scheme dominated by Stockholm.
